guide.title: Version Control Guide

baselineMeaning.title: What is the baseline version
baselineMeaning.body: When version control is enabled, the system saves the current requirement space as the "baseline" commit on main. A baseline is immutable: it records the full model at a point in time, for later branching, comparison, and traceability.

whenToBranch.title: When to create a branch
whenToBranch.body: Create a branch from any commit or main when you want to explore alternatives in parallel or make a large change without affecting the mainline. Branches are isolated from each other and can be committed and compared at any time.

mainProtection.title: Why main is protected
mainProtection.body: main is the project's mainline and forbids direct commits. Every change entering main must go through a Merge Request and receive at least one approval from a non-author admin/owner, keeping history traceable and changes reviewable.

mrApproval.title: Merge Request approval rules
mrApproval.body: A Merge Request needs at least one approval from a non-author admin/owner. If the source branch gains new commits or the target branch advances, existing approvals are automatically invalidated and must be re-given. Unresolved conflicts or required comments block the merge.

unsupportedGitFeatures.title: Git features not yet supported
unsupportedGitFeatures.body: This version control does not offer rebase, cherry-pick, tags, remote repository sync, or command-line compatibility. Organize changes through branches and merge requests instead.

guide.collapsedHint: Click to expand core operations such as baseline snapshots, branch policies, MR reviews, and rollbacks...

revert.title: Version Rollback Tips
revert.body: Select any historical commit and click 'Rollback to this commit'. The system will generate a revert commit on the current branch and restore all specification entities with full auditability.

stages.title: Stage Progression
stages.body: Each branch independently advances What (Actors/Features) → Flow (Workflows) → Scope (Scope acceptance). Interactive prototypes can be compiled once all prerequisite stages are met.

merge.title: Semantic 3-Way Merge
merge.body: Merge runs diff and merge at the semantic entity and attribute level. When conflicts occur, select options per entity without manual code edits.

systemGuide.title: Workbench User Guide & Specification Manual
systemGuide.subtitle: Complete manual for formal specifications, branch collaboration, version rollback, and prototype compilation

lifecycle.title: Full Specification Evolution Lifecycle
lifecycle.summary: RequirementSpace employs a formal specification architecture that transforms unstructured requirements into high-fidelity structured models. It strictly enforces a 3-stage progression gate check before enabling interactive prototype compilation.

highlights.title: Strict 3-Stage Progression
highlights.desc: Specifications must advance sequentially through What (Actors & Features) → Flow (Business Flows) → Scope (Scope & Acceptance). Each stage builds on the previous one.

highlights.title: Isolated Branch Workspace State
highlights.desc: Each branch maintains an entirely isolated workspace model and stage progression status. Progress on one branch never affects other branches.

highlights.title: Shadow Preview vs. Real Prototype
highlights.desc: When prerequisite stages are incomplete, the preview displays a shadow skeleton. Once all 3 stages are fully ready, sandbox prototype compilation is unlocked.

highlights.title: Formal Traceability Graph
highlights.desc: Actors, features, flow steps, business objects, Gherkin scenarios, and acceptance criteria are linked via logical UUIDs, supporting bidirectional traceability.

steps.title: Stage 1: What - Actors & Features
steps.desc: Identify system actors, organize hierarchical feature trees, assign KANO value categories, and confirm AI assumptions.

steps.title: Stage 2: Flow - Business Flow Orchestration
steps.desc: Design swimlane diagrams for core features, assign acting roles to steps, and define input/output business objects.

steps.title: Stage 3: Scope - Scope & Acceptance
steps.desc: Determine In-Scope/Out-of-Scope boundaries, write executable Gherkin scenarios (Given-When-Then), and pass gate check.

steps.title: Stage 4: Interactive Prototype Compilation
steps.desc: Trigger sandbox compilation once prerequisite specifications are complete, generating a high-fidelity interactive prototype.

faqs.q: Why does the preview page still show a shadow skeleton after completing the What stage?
faqs.a: Because interactive prototypes depend on complete actors, features, flows, and Gherkin scenarios. All three stages (What, Flow, Scope) must be completed before compilation begins.

faqs.q: Why do different branches show different preview states?
faqs.a: Each branch is an independent requirement workspace. For instance, the main branch might have just finished What, while a feature branch has finished all 3 stages.

guidance.title: Read Guidance, Resolve Issues & Advance
guidance.summary: If you are unsure what to do next, start with Pending Issues and Next Suggestion in Overview, then open the relevant stage. Guidance at the top of each stage page explains what is missing, what can be refined and when you can advance.

highlights.title: Find Work to Do in Overview
highlights.desc: Pending Issues shows specific problems and may also contain a Suggestion to refine card. Issue cards are marked High Risk, Needs Resolution or Notice and can be opened for details. Refinement suggestions help improve the model; their presence does not necessarily prevent stage progression.

highlights.title: Start with Next Suggestion
highlights.desc: Next Suggestion in Overview recommends a current action. When progression is available, it displays Enter How Stage, Enter Scope Stage or Enter Preview Stage. Stage pages also offer action buttons, such as generating content, reviewing domain rules or completing workflow steps.

highlights.title: Expand Issues & Quality Hints on a Stage Page
highlights.desc: Expand Pending Issues or Workspace Health at the top of a stage page to read the details. Items with related objects can be opened for details or to highlight those objects. Buttons beside issues start the relevant action. Workspace Health hints can be addressed as needed.

highlights.title: Use Stage Guidance to Decide Whether to Proceed
highlights.desc: The left navigation shows stage status, pending counts and notices about blocking issues or suggestions to refine. If the stage is incomplete, follow the stated reason to add missing content. When requirements are met and no blocking items remain, the stage page shows Current stage is complete and a button to advance.

highlights.title: When Model Readiness Verification Failed Appears
highlights.desc: Attempting a stage transition or preview generation may open Model Readiness Verification Failed. The dialog explains what must be completed or confirmed for this operation and provides action buttons or manual repair guidance. Address the items, then request the original operation again.

steps.title: Choose an Issue or Suggestion in Overview
steps.desc: Read a card in Pending Issues or select Next Suggestion. Opening an issue card takes you to the relevant page and shows issue details. Selecting a suggestion opens the relevant action entry or performs its recommended operation.

steps.title: Complete the Model Using the Available Action
steps.desc: Expand Pending Issues on the stage page and use the action beside the relevant explanation. If automatic handling is unavailable, edit the related actor, feature, scenario, rule or workflow manually.

steps.title: Review & Apply AI Proposals
steps.desc: If candidates or a draft appear, review the content before adopting a suitable candidate or confirming the draft. Reject unsuitable candidates. Generating a proposal alone does not resolve the problem; address any reported conflict first.

steps.title: Diagnose Further as Needed
steps.desc: When What or How offers Diagnose requirements space, run AI diagnosis for further refinement suggestions. The button changes to Re-diagnose when related suggestions exist. Read the results and decide what to add; you do not need to complete every refinement suggestion before advancing.

steps.title: Confirm the Guidance & Advance
steps.desc: Use the stage transition entry when it appears. If a readiness dialog opens, address the listed causes and try again. If an operation fails, read the error and use the retry or manual action available on that page.

faqs.q: Why are refinement suggestions shown alongside pending issues?
faqs.a: This area brings together content that needs attention. Issues describe specific gaps or errors, while refinement suggestions propose further improvements. Read each card label, explanation and action; refinement suggestions need not all be treated as blockers.

faqs.q: Why can I not advance when there are no pending issues?
faqs.a: Required content may still be missing, a prerequisite stage may be incomplete or analysis may still be running. Read the stage notice and navigation lock reason, complete the requirements and try again.

faqs.q: Why are there suggestions when an advance button is available?
faqs.a: Nonblocking refinement suggestions may remain after required conditions are met. You can advance or continue refining the current stage. Next Action and Stage Transition can appear together on a stage page.

faqs.q: Why does an issue remain after I generate a draft?
faqs.a: Drafts and candidates must be reviewed and applied to the model. Adopt a candidate or confirm a draft, resolve any conflict, then check the updated status or request the original operation again.

faqs.q: Does Ignore change the model?
faqs.a: No. Ignoring stops displaying that issue or quality hint but does not add missing content or change model relationships. Ignore a hint if it is inapplicable to your requirements. Mandatory modeling content still needs to be completed.

faqs.q: What do Cancel and Continue anyway mean in the readiness dialog?
faqs.a: Cancel stops this operation so you can return to editing. Continue anyway attempts to proceed past the listed blocking items without repairing the content. A first transition still cannot skip mandatory content, a locked stage or analysis in progress. Stage transitions that bypass blockers leave an audit record.

ai_assistant.title: AI Assistant: Q&A, Changes & Conversational Creation
ai_assistant.summary: In a project workspace, open AI Assistant using the purple sparkle button at the bottom right. Use Q&A to understand existing requirements and Modify to change an existing object. To add an object, use the conversational creation entry on its page. Model changes are drafted first and applied after review and confirmation.

highlights.title: Open, Collapse & Move the Assistant
highlights.desc: Expand the assistant with the floating button at the bottom right and collapse it with the minus button in its header. Drag the floating button or window header to keep the model visible.

highlights.title: Choose the Q&A Scope
highlights.desc: In Q&A, Scope offers the current stage or Entire Workspace. Selecting an object on the page also allows questions about that object. Changing pages or selecting an object resets the scope selection, so check the displayed scope before sending.

highlights.title: Ask About Existing Requirements
highlights.desc: Type a question and send it with the send button or Enter. Use Shift+Enter for a new line. Ask about a feature responsibility, the meaning of a workflow or content that needs attention in the current stage. Answers explain the project model and do not themselves change it.

highlights.title: Modify an Existing Object Through Conversation
highlights.desc: Select a supported object, such as an actor, feature, workflow or business object. Switch to Modify, check the Object name and select Start Editing. Describe the desired changes and answer follow-up questions. When ready, choose Generate Edit Draft or Continue Chatting.

highlights.title: Review the Before & After Changes
highlights.desc: Preview Changes shows the original and proposed content and may include a rationale. Select Confirm Changes to save and refresh the workspace. If the proposal is unsuitable, select Discard and start editing again.

highlights.title: Create Objects from Their Page Entries
highlights.desc: What offers conversational entries for adding actors, feature modules and child features. How offers entries for creating workflows and business objects. Describe the new object, answer follow-up questions and select Generate Draft. Review the preview and select Confirm & Create, or continue chatting or discard the draft.

steps.title: Open the Assistant & Choose a Scope
steps.desc: Open the assistant on the relevant stage and select Q&A. To ask about one object, select it on the page first and check the object name displayed in Scope.

steps.title: Ask to Understand the Existing Model
steps.desc: Describe what you want to understand, such as which actors use a feature or what a workflow accomplishes. Read the answer before deciding whether a change is needed.

steps.title: Select an Object & Start Editing
steps.desc: Select the object to change, switch to Modify, check its name and select Start Editing. If the button is unavailable, follow the prompt to select a supported object.

steps.title: Describe the Changes & Add Detail
steps.desc: State the content to change and the expected result, such as adding responsibility for reviewing refund requests to an actor. Answer follow-up questions. When the generation entry appears, generate an edit draft or continue chatting.

steps.title: Review Changes & Confirm or Discard
steps.desc: Compare each original and proposed value before selecting Confirm Changes. Select Discard if you do not want to apply it. Retry generation if it fails; if confirmation fails, read the error and retry confirmation in the preview.

steps.title: Use Page Entries to Add New Objects
steps.desc: Start a new object conversation from the relevant page entry. After generating a draft, check its name, description and any displayed relationships, then select Confirm & Create and inspect the saved object.

faqs.q: Will requesting changes in Q&A save them directly?
faqs.a: No. Q&A explains existing project content. To change the model, select an object, use Modify, generate an edit draft and review and confirm it.

faqs.q: Why is Start Editing unavailable?
faqs.a: Modification requires a specific supported object. Entire Workspace, the current stage or an unsupported object cannot start an edit. Check the object name, prompt and button state in the assistant.

faqs.q: Can the floating assistant add new objects directly?
faqs.a: The floating assistant provides Q&A and changes to existing objects. To create actors, features, workflows or business objects, use the conversational creation entry on What or How.

faqs.q: Can I continue the same conversation after generating an edit draft?
faqs.a: Before generation, use Continue Chatting to add detail. Once Preview Changes opens, the available actions are Confirm Changes and Discard. Discarding requires starting a new edit.

faqs.q: What happens when I collapse, clear Q&A or switch modes?
faqs.a: Collapsing only folds the window. Clear in Q&A removes the displayed question and answer history without changing the model. Switching from Modify to Q&A resets the edit process and discards an unconfirmed edit draft, so decide whether to save first.

faqs.q: What if an answer or draft does not match my requirements?
faqs.a: Ask a more specific question and check the Q&A scope. Before generation, continue chatting to clarify changes or creation details. Discard unsuitable drafts. If a request, generation or confirmation fails, retry using the available entry; a failure message does not mean the content was saved.

what.title: What Stage: Actors & Features
what.summary: The What stage establishes the foundation of requirements engineering, defining system actor boundaries, hierarchical feature trees, and KANO value classifications.

highlights.title: Actor Roles & Boundaries
highlights.desc: Define real users or external systems interacting with the product, specifying descriptions and permission boundaries.

highlights.title: Hierarchical Feature Decomposition
highlights.desc: Deconstruct product capabilities into root and nested feature nodes with detailed descriptions and dependencies.

highlights.title: KANO Value Categorization
highlights.desc: Classify features into Must-be, One-dimensional, and Attractive attributes to guide project roadmap priorities.

highlights.title: AI Assumption Confirmation
highlights.desc: Assumptions inferred by AI during document analysis are marked as pending and can be batch-reviewed in the Decision Center.

steps.title: Add & Confirm System Actors
steps.desc: Define system roles in the actors panel or approve AI-inferred actor assumptions.

steps.title: Build Feature Trees
steps.desc: Create root and child features, maintaining structured descriptions and parent-child hierarchies.

steps.title: Evaluate KANO & Gate Check
steps.desc: Classify features and complete checklist requirements to unlock the Flow stage.

faqs.q: How do I edit or remove a feature node?
faqs.a: Select the node in the feature tree to edit its properties in the right inspector panel or click delete in the toolbar.

flow.title: How Stage: Rule-Driven Flow Modeling
flow.summary: The How stage starts by discovering and reviewing domain rules, then uses them to constrain flows, steps, branches, and transitions. Business objects are maintained in each flow through step input/output relationships and field attributes.

highlights.title: Dedicated Domain Rule View
highlights.desc: Discover or rediscover rules with AI, add them manually, and inspect their hierarchy, confirmation status, and linked objects in card or compact view.

highlights.title: Rule-Driven Flow Generation
highlights.desc: Domain rules are a prerequisite for flow generation. Steps and branches can also link to specific rules, preserving traceability from requirement evidence to execution paths.

highlights.title: Branch and Path Modeling
highlights.desc: Arrange actor actions, system actions, and decision branches on the flow canvas; maintain conditions and default branches, then focus the main or alternative routes with path projection.

highlights.title: Business Object Attributes in Context
highlights.desc: Each flow summarizes its involved business objects and shows how they participate through step input/output relationships and field attributes.

steps.title: Discover and Review Domain Rules
steps.desc: Use AI rule discovery or add rules manually, then check each statement, confirmation status, and source links.

steps.title: Generate or Create a Business Flow
steps.desc: Once at least one domain rule exists, generate flows with AI or create a flow manually and associate the relevant features.

steps.title: Arrange Steps, Branches, and Rules
steps.desc: Add typed steps, assign actors, connect steps on the canvas, and define branch conditions, default paths, and linked rules.

steps.title: Maintain Object Attributes in Each Flow
steps.desc: Use the Involved Business Objects area inside an expanded flow to manage objects and field attributes, then assign step input/output relationships.

faqs.q: Why are domain rules required before flow generation?
faqs.a: Domain rules provide constraints for flow steps and branches. Generate or add at least one rule in the rule view before generating flows.

faqs.q: How do I maintain the business objects used by a flow?
faqs.a: Expand a flow and use its Involved Business Objects area to create or select an object. Click an object to edit its name, description, and fields; set input/output relationships on the relevant flow steps.

faqs.q: How do I create and refine branches?
faqs.a: Drag from a step port to a target step on the flow canvas. Select the transition to edit its condition, evaluation order, default-branch setting, and linked domain rules.

scope.title: Scope Stage: Scope & Acceptance Criteria
scope.summary: The Scope stage establishes product acceptance criteria through rigorous Gherkin scenarios and scope boundaries, unlocking prototype compilation.

highlights.title: Standardized Gherkin Scenarios
highlights.desc: Structure testable acceptance criteria using Given (prerequisites), When (triggers), and Then (expected outcomes).

highlights.title: Scope Boundary Definition
highlights.desc: Classify features as In-Scope (current release) or Out-of-Scope (deferred) with detailed rationale.

highlights.title: Precise Acceptance Mapping
highlights.desc: Bind acceptance rules to specific features, business objects, and steps to eliminate ambiguity.

highlights.title: Checks Before Entering Preview
highlights.desc: When entering Preview, the system checks prerequisite content. If Model Readiness Verification Failed appears, complete or confirm the listed content and try again.

steps.title: Define Feature Scope
steps.desc: Mark features as In-Scope or Out-of-Scope and document business rationale.

steps.title: Author Gherkin Scenarios
steps.desc: Write Given-When-Then rules for key scenarios, covering both positive flows and edge cases.

steps.title: Confirm Stage Status & Enter Preview
steps.desc: After completing scope decisions, check stage status and use Enter Preview Stage when available. If checks fail, address the listed causes and try again.

faqs.q: How do Gherkin scenarios manifest in the prototype?
faqs.a: The compilation engine maps Given-When-Then rules directly into interactive prototype event handlers, validation logic, and view transitions.

preview.title: Shadow Preview & Prototype Sandbox
preview.summary: Provides a live sandbox environment compiling formal specifications into clickable, interactive high-fidelity prototype views.

highlights.title: Dual-State Presentation
highlights.desc: Displays a shadow skeleton when prerequisite stages are in progress, and an interactive prototype when all 3 stages are complete.

highlights.title: Bidirectional Traceability
highlights.desc: Clicking any UI component in the prototype inspects its underlying feature, actor permissions, and Gherkin scenarios.

highlights.title: Sandbox Hot-Reloading
highlights.desc: When specification models are updated and committed, the sandbox automatically triggers hot incremental compilation.

faqs.q: What should I do if a prototype interaction doesn't match expectations?
faqs.a: Navigate back to the respective What/Flow/Scope stage to update actor attributes, flow links, or Gherkin assertions, then commit changes.

branching.title: Branch Management & Protection
branching.summary: A Git-like branch management system supporting parallel exploration across team members with strict main branch protection and workspace isolation.

highlights.title: Protected Main Branch
highlights.desc: The main branch represents the production baseline. Direct unreviewed writes are prohibited; changes must be merged via Merge Requests.

highlights.title: Isolated Feature Branches
highlights.desc: Branch off from any historical commit or branch to explore designs with fully independent workspace models and stage progression.

highlights.title: Lossless Branch Switching
highlights.desc: Switch branches seamlessly from the top bar or repository overview without losing uncommitted progress.

highlights.title: Standard Branch Naming
highlights.desc: Recommended naming prefixes include feature/xxx, fix/xxx, and explore/xxx.

steps.title: Create Branch from Baseline
steps.desc: Select the source branch or commit in the repository overview and click 'Create Branch'.

steps.title: Iterate in Branch Workspace
steps.desc: Switch to your branch to advance stages, edit entities, or orchestrate flows independently.

steps.title: Commit Changes & Open MR
steps.desc: Commit workspace changes and open a Merge Request to merge back into the target branch.

faqs.q: Why can't I edit specifications directly on the main branch?
faqs.a: Main is the protected baseline for the entire team. Create a feature branch to make modifications and merge via MR review.

commit_revert.title: Commit Graph & Version Rollback
commit_revert.summary: Every commit seals an immutable full-state snapshot (state_json) with SHA-256 integrity; supports 1-click safe rollback for any commit or merge commit.

highlights.title: Deterministic Full Snapshots
highlights.desc: Unlike text-based diff patches, each commit records a complete normalized specification graph, ensuring rock-solid consistency.

highlights.title: Git-Style Revert Commit
highlights.desc: Clicking 'Revert to this commit' restores workspace models from historical snapshots and generates a new revert commit to maintain linear history.

highlights.title: Merge Commit Rollback Support
highlights.desc: Merge commits can also be safely reverted back to their pre-merge baseline, guarding against unintended merges.

highlights.title: Lossless Historical Safety
highlights.desc: Since rollback creates a new commit, all previous commits remain intact in the graph and can be re-reverted at any time.

steps.title: Locate Target Historical Commit
steps.desc: Select the target historical version in the commit timeline or commit graph.

steps.title: Click 'Revert to this commit'
steps.desc: Click the revert button in the right commit inspector to open the confirmation dialog.

steps.title: Confirm & Generate Revert Commit
steps.desc: Review the commit message and confirm; the system resets workspace entities and advances branch Head.

faqs.q: Will rolling back delete my existing commit history?
faqs.a: No. The system strictly adheres to immutable history principles. Rollback creates a new Revert commit, keeping all historical records safe.

merge_request.title: Merge Requests & Semantic 3-Way Merge
merge_request.summary: Merge Requests (MR) facilitate collaborative review with semantic diffs, inline comment threads, and a dedicated 3-way conflict resolution workbench.

highlights.title: Entity-Level Semantic Diff
highlights.desc: Intelligently contrasts added, modified, and removed attributes for actors, features, flows, and scenarios rather than raw text lines.

highlights.title: Approval & Inline Reviews
highlights.desc: Submit Approve or Request Changes decisions and leave blocking inline review comments on specific entity fields.

highlights.title: 2-Column Conflict Resolution Workbench
highlights.desc: When concurrent modifications occur on the same attribute, an interactive workbench allows item-by-item selection of source vs. target values.

highlights.title: Automatic Post-Merge Refresh
highlights.desc: Upon successful merge, the system immediately refreshes branches, commit graphs, MR status, and current workspace without manual F5.

steps.title: Create Merge Request
steps.desc: Click 'New MR', choose source and target branches (e.g. main), and provide title and description.

steps.title: Review Diff & Submit Approval
steps.desc: Inspect semantic diffs in the 'Changes' tab and leave comments or submit Approve decisions in 'Overview & Reviews'.

steps.title: Execute Merge & Resolve Conflicts
steps.desc: Click 'Merge' when approved and unblocked. If semantic conflicts exist, resolve them in the interactive modal.

faqs.q: Why is the Merge button disabled after creating an MR?
faqs.a: Check that: 1) At least one maintainer has submitted an Approved review; 2) All blocking required comments are resolved; 3) Source branch has new commits.

collaboration.title: Team Collaboration & Decision Center
collaboration.summary: Provides role-based member permission control, AI decision task assignment, and real-time notification feeds for agile teams.

highlights.title: 4-Tier Role Permissions
highlights.desc: Supports fine-grained permissions for Owner, Admin, Member, and Viewer roles.

highlights.title: Decision Task Center
highlights.desc: AI-inferred assumptions, conflict resolutions, and transition reviews are assigned as actionable tasks.

highlights.title: Real-Time Notification Feed
highlights.desc: Receive real-time alerts for task assignments, MR reviews, and merge events with 1-click mark-as-read.

faqs.q: How do I invite new members to a project?
faqs.a: Project Owners or Admins can click the 'Members' icon in the top navigation bar, enter member emails, and assign roles.
